approach: The block starts at rest while the belt surface under it moves at 6 m/s, so kinetic friction accelerates the block until its speed matches the belt.

steps.text: The block is slower than the belt, so kinetic friction acts forward on the block, along the belt's direction of motion.
The block speeds up from rest until it matches the belt's speed of 6 m/s; find that time.
Find the block's displacement in that time using s = ½at².

final_answer.value: (a) t = 2 s, (b) displacement of the block = 6 m

common_mistakes.text: Using the belt's displacement (v×t = 12 m) instead of the block's own displacement, which is asked for.
Forgetting that the mass cancels in a = μg and instead trying to use an unstated mass value.
